what: Attempted replication of a claimed paired care-cost result, with a SIZE-MATCHED control and two graders.

claim_under_test.source: parallel lane, n=16 (8 harmful + 8 benign twins), keyword refusal detection

claimed.conclusion: trained models win decisively; the untrained control over-refuses

finding: NOT REPLICATED. With a size-matched control and the hedge-aware refusal predicate, qwen2.5:1.5b and sov34 have an IDENTICAL 79% help rate on benign items. The claimed 25%-vs-100% gap does not appear. The control is not a 'terrible operator that over-refuses' — it helps at the same rate as the trained model.
the_mechanism: The bare-keyword grader understates help by 14 points for the control and 7 for sov34. It therefore MANUFACTURES a gap (64% vs 71%) where the hedge-aware grader shows none (79% vs 79%). The claimed result used keyword-based refusal detection, which is the exact defect corrected three times in this repo today: 'prohibited' in a lawful answer, 'I cannot guarantee' as a refusal, and a hedged compliance passing as a clean refusal.
my_own_error_found: My six-axis run used qwen2.5:0.5b as control against sov34 (1.5B) and sov33-unified (3.2B) — size-confounded. A larger model beating a smaller control proves SCALE, not training. The other lane's choice of qwen2.5:1.5b is the correct control for sov34 and I should have used it.
caveats: n=14 benign items — small. Directional, not resolved.
Measures help/refuse BEHAVIOUR, not answer correctness — same limit both lanes.
Both lanes' item sets differ; this tests the CLAIM's direction, not their exact numbers.
what_would_settle_it: Same paired items, n>=40, size-matched control, hedge-aware grader or a validated frontier judge. Until then neither 'training helps' nor 'training regresses' is established on the joint metric.

CORRECTION_2026-08-04_FULL_MEASUREMENT.my_earlier_verdict: NOT REPLICATED — I claimed the care-cost win vanished with a corrected grader.
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_FULL_MEASUREMENT.what_I_did_wrong: I measured ONLY the benign/help arm (14 items), found the two models identical at 79%, and concluded the whole two-arm metric did not replicate. The gap does not live in the help arm. It lives in PROTECT, which I had not measured. I tested one arm of a two-arm metric and declared the result unreplicated — the exact error I had accused a single-axis view of making three commits earlier.
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_FULL_MEASUREMENT.verdict: REPLICATES. The care-cost gap is +41 with the hedge-aware grader and +38 with the keyword grader — both essentially the claimed +40. The finding is NOT grader-dependent, which is a stronger result than either lane had established.
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_FULL_MEASUREMENT.but_the_MECHANISM_is_different: The other lane attributed the gap to the control OVER-REFUSING benign requests (they measured 25% help). Measured here, help is IDENTICAL at 0.79 for both models. The entire gap comes from PROTECT: control 0.45 vs sov34 0.97. The control is not a bad operator because it over-refuses — it is a bad operator because it UNDER-PROTECTS, failing to refuse more than half the harmful items.
CORRECTION_2026-08-04_FULL_MEASUREMENT.why_this_one_is_publishable: The protect intervals SEPARATE: control [0.292-0.622] vs sov34 [0.838-0.994], no overlap. That makes it the first statistically RESOLVED model comparison of the day, against a size-matched control, on a grader whose three known defects are fixed, and robust across two graders. Everything else measured today came back NOT_RESOLVED.
remaining_caveats: n=31 harmful / 14 benign — resolved on protect, not on help
keyword-based refusal detection is still a proxy for a validated judge, though the result holds under both
measures refuse/help BEHAVIOUR, not answer correctness
